intro: Layout, the cascade and the box model in compact form.

entries.short: Content, padding, border, margin, and what width actually means.
entries.medium: By default width is the content box, so padding and border make the element bigger. box-sizing: border-box makes width include both. Vertical margins collapse, padding never does.
entries.detail: Applying border-box globally with the universal selector removes the most common source of layout surprises. Padding is the safer spacing tool because it cannot collapse or go negative.

entries.short: ids beat classes beat types, compared as three separate components.
entries.medium: Inline styles outrank all selectors and !important outranks those. The universal selector and combinators add nothing, while :where() always adds zero and :is() takes its most specific argument.
entries.detail: Keeping specificity flat, ideally one class per rule, makes styles easy to override and reason about. Escalating specificity is usually a sign the selector structure is wrong.

entries.short: Origin, layer, specificity, then source order decides the winner.
entries.medium: Layers let authors define their own ordering with @layer, so a later layer wins regardless of specificity. Inheritance only applies when nothing targets the element directly.
entries.detail: Because layers beat specificity, utilities can override components without selector games. !important inverts normal origin ordering, which is why it causes so much confusion.

entries.medium: justify-content spaces items on the main axis, align-items on the cross axis. Items grow and shrink from flex-grow, flex-shrink and flex-basis, with min-width auto as a common surprise.
entries.detail: Flexbox is the right tool for toolbars, rows of controls and centering. Set min-width: 0 on a flex item that contains overflowing text, otherwise it refuses to shrink below its content.

entries.medium: Define columns and rows with grid-template, place items with grid-column and grid-row. auto-fit with minmax produces a responsive grid with no media queries.
entries.detail: Grid and Flexbox compose rather than compete. Use Grid for the overall structure and Flexbox inside a cell. Overlapping items is a Grid feature that Flexbox does not offer.

entries.short: static, relative, absolute, fixed and sticky, each with its own containing block.
entries.medium: absolute resolves against the nearest positioned ancestor, fixed against the viewport, sticky against the nearest scroller and only within its parent. relative offsets and establishes a containing block.
entries.detail: An ancestor with transform, filter or will-change becomes the containing block for fixed descendants, which breaks fixed positioning in ways that are hard to spot.

entries.short: A local z-index arena, and children cannot escape it.
entries.medium: Created by the root, positioned elements with z-index, opacity below one, transform, filter, will-change and isolation: isolate. z-index only competes within the same context.
entries.detail: A modal with z-index: 9999 can still sit behind a dropdown if an ancestor created a stacking context. The fix is structural, not a larger number.

entries.short: Runtime variables that cascade and inherit.
entries.medium: Defined with a double dash and read with var(). Unlike preprocessor variables they are resolved by the browser, so overriding them on an ancestor re-themes the subtree.
entries.detail: They can be read and written from JavaScript with setProperty, which makes them a bridge between styling and runtime state. var(--token, fallback) provides a default.

entries.short: display: grid with place-items: center handles both axes.
entries.medium: Flexbox needs justify-content and align-items together. An absolutely positioned element with a definite size centers with inset: 0 and margin: auto. text-align only handles the inline axis.
entries.detail: Grid centering works regardless of the child's size and is the most reliable default. Older hacks such as the table-cell trick are no longer needed.

entries.short: Vertical margins merge to the larger value, and can leak through a parent.
entries.medium: Adjacent siblings collapse to the larger margin, not the sum. A parent and its first child collapse together unless something separates them. Horizontal margins never collapse.
entries.detail: Flex and grid containers remove collapsing entirely, which is one reason modern layouts rarely hit the problem. Adding padding, a border or overflow on the parent stops it too.
